name: Cigarette diet

lead: The cigarette diet refers to using cigarettes to reduce hunger and eat less, a practice with a long history in fashion and advertising. People who do it are aiming for a lower body weight and a leaner face and physique.

Nicotine reduces appetite and increases energy expenditure, and most research finds smokers weigh less than non-smokers. The same research documents substantial health harms from smoking, which are the main focus of medical bodies.

paras: In general terms, people replace or delay meals with cigarettes. Forum users describe nicotine as making food restriction easier, while others describe it as harming training motivation and diet.

Nicotine is highly addictive, with withdrawal lasting days to weeks. Smoke exposes users to carbon monoxide and carcinogens, raises heart rate and blood pressure, and is linked to heart disease, lung disease and cancer. Weight often rises after quitting.

chain: Lower calorie intake and higher energy expenditure
angle.text: Users aim to eat less by suppressing appetite with nicotine, producing a lower body weight and leaner look. The effect on weight is documented in research, alongside substantial health harms.

lead: The cigarette diet is the use of smoking as an appetite suppressant to keep body weight down. People pursue it for appearance: a leaner face, slimmer body and lower weight. It appears in the fringe category of looksmaxxing and bodybuilding discussion, usually as a cautionary or contested topic. [1][2]

Research supports the underlying pharmacology. Nicotine decreases hunger and food consumption and increases energy expenditure, and the majority of studies find it reduces body weight; a proposed mechanism involves receptors on POMC neurons in the melanocortin system. [1]

The same pharmacology comes with documented harm. Nicotine is highly addictive, raises heart rate and blood pressure and constricts blood vessels, and cigarette smoke contains other toxic substances such as carbon monoxide. Tobacco-specific nitrosamines formed in processing are carcinogenic. [1]
infobox: Tobacco legal for adults in most countries

paras: The practice treats cigarettes as a substitute for food or a way to delay eating. Forum discussion shows both sides: one T Nation poster reasoned that a daily nicotine habit would make limiting food intake much easier, while another described cigarettes as undermining diet and lifting motivation. [2][3]

Nicotine decreases hunger and food intake and increases energy expenditure, and most studies in the literature report reduced body weight, although some animal work found gain under certain feeding patterns. [1]

Nicotine dependence includes tolerance and withdrawal that peaks within one to three days and may last several weeks. [1] Nicotine raises heart rate and blood pressure, and long-term use is associated with hypertension; smoke also delivers carbon monoxide. [1] In pregnancy, smoking is linked to higher risk of miscarriage and stillbirth and lower birth weight. [1]
No studies found testing smoking as a deliberate weight-loss diet. Broader research on nicotine and body weight is summarised above. [1]

lore.intro: The topic surfaces occasionally in T Nation threads on dieting, with mixed views. [2][3]
